clue.text: Organisation with source of mature prairie beef

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, an organisation

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, so only its first letter is taken

parts.note: a prairie is a broad grassy plain

explanation.surface: A company deals in grass-fed beef from mature cattle raised on the prairie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' looks like the meat the organisation sells, but it is the verb meaning to grumble. 'source of' takes M from 'mature'.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef is slang for grumbling or protesting about something.

clue.text: Marsh stifles river plant

indicators.note: to stifle is to smother, so the marsh word wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a fen is low marshy land, as in the East Anglian Fens
R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: A swamp chokes the life out of a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stifles' puts R inside FEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A fern is a green, leafy, flowerless plant that spreads by spores.

clue.text: Explanation drawn from article on circle line

parts.note: the definite article in English grammar
the letter O is round, like a circle
RY is a crossword abbreviation for railway, a line

explanation.surface: Someone works out a theory from a newspaper article about London's Circle line.
explanation.walkthrough: The Circle line is a London Underground route, but here 'circle' and 'line' are separate pieces: O and RY (railway).
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a proposed account of why something happens.

clue.text: Injured badger found outside the Spanish capital

indicators.note: being outside something means surrounding it, so the anagram goes round the next piece
something injured is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A wounded badger turns up on the edge of Madrid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Spanish capital' wants to be Madrid, but 'the Spanish' is wordplay and 'capital' alone defines; 'Injured' makes B GRADE, which 'found outside' wraps round the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgrade is the capital city of Serbia.

clue.text: Treated and, for example, covered by newly-developed antidote

indicators.note: being covered by means being enclosed, so the anagram wraps round the abbreviation
something newly developed has been reshaped, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: EG is the short form of exempli gratia, for example

explanation.surface: A patient was treated with a newly developed antidote, among other things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treated' looks medical but means dealt or bargained with, as in treating with an enemy; 'covered by' sits the abbreviation inside the reworked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To treat with someone is to bargain or hold talks, as diplomats do.

clue.text: Cancel river crossing permit

indicators.note: a river crossing something stretches across it, so the river word goes round the other piece

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain, flowing through Chester and also Aberdeen
to let is to permit or allow

explanation.surface: Someone scraps a permit to cross a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a British river; 'crossing' has the river span the permit word.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete is to strike out or erase, cancelling what was written.

clue.text: Return in tie as one

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the word for tie

parts.note: to tether is to tie up an animal
to return is to go back, so the word go is written backwards

explanation.surface: A player returns to the match after a tie and everyone celebrates in unison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return' means 'go back', read cryptically as the word go written backwards; 'in' places that inside the word for tie.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something as one means doing it jointly, in unison.

clue.text: Staggered by fish-eating bolshie

indicators.note: something eating another takes it inside, so the first word wraps round the second

parts.note: bolshie is British slang for rebellious, from Bolshevik, so a Red
an eel is a snake-like fish

explanation.surface: Someone is staggered by a rebellious type who eats fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bolshie' is British slang for awkward or rebellious, from Bolshevik, hence a communist colour; 'eating' has that colour swallow the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To have reeled is to have lurched about unsteadily, tottering.

clue.text: One backs one for the team

definitions.text: One backs one for the team

parts.words: One backs one for the team
parts.note: the figure one placed behind another figure one gives the two-digit number that names a side in football or cricket

explanation.surface: One player supports a teammate for the good of the side.
explanation.walkthrough: Write 1 and put another 1 behind it to get 11, the number of players in a football or cricket side.
explanation.definitionFit: A side in football or cricket fields this many players, so the number names the team.

clue.text: Bites back in turn

indicators.note: back means the word nips is read backwards

parts.note: nips are small bites

explanation.surface: A dog bites back when its turn comes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses NIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: A spin is a turn or rotation, or a short trip out.

clue.text: Kitchen wear involves ego, cooked without one

indicators.note: letters that are cooked are cooked up into something new, so they are rearranged
without means the letter for one is taken out

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Cooking in the kitchen means involving your ego, minus anyone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes I out of INVOLVES, and 'cooked' rearranges what is left with EGO.
explanation.definitionFit: These padded gloves are worn in the kitchen to handle hot dishes.

clue.text: An old car cut into bird

indicators.note: into puts the first piece inside the bird

parts.note: a jay is a bird of the crow family
to lop is to cut off, as branches

explanation.surface: A vintage car crashed into a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' is a verb hiding as an adjective on the car; 'into' sends it inside the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A jalopy is a battered, worn-out old motor vehicle.

clue.text: Workers work a long time, and time is to accept victory in Europe

parts.note: OP is short for opus, Latin for a work
an era is a long period of history

indicators.note: to accept something is to take it in, so the word is wraps round the next piece

parts.note: VE stands for Victory in Europe, as in VE Day in 1945

explanation.surface: Labourers put in a long shift, with time needed to celebrate VE Day.
explanation.walkthrough: VE Day (8 May 1945) marked victory in Europe; 'to accept' has the word is take those two letters in.
explanation.definitionFit: Operatives are workers, especially those on a factory floor.

clue.text: Formerly a worker underground, he demands answers

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-wife
a miner works underground, digging coal

explanation.surface: An ex-miner now spends his days asking questions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he demands answers' is a description rather than a synonym: the person who sets an exam paper.
explanation.definitionFit: An examiner sets questions and expects candidates to answer them.

clue.text: Provoke the French on poverty

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the French word follows the other piece in the across answer

parts.note: need is poverty or want
le is the masculine French word for the

explanation.surface: Poverty in France provokes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' usually means 'about'; in an across answer it means 'placed after'.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to irritate or goad them.

clue.text: Shining desire to wake up? Not quite

parts.note: lust is strong desire

indicators.note: not quite means the word is left one letter short at its end

parts.note: to rouse someone is to wake them up

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the desire to wake up is shining through, and decides not quite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' drops the last letter E from ROUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustrous means glossy, gleaming with a soft light.

clue.text: Badger's view across the road

indicators.note: across means the looking word stretches over the next piece

parts.note: to peer is to look closely, to view
ST is the abbreviation for street, a road

explanation.surface: A badger peers across the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' is the verb meaning to nag, not the animal; 'across' has the looking word stretch over the street abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to harass them with repeated demands.

clue.text: Gave a performance while plastered

explanation.surface: An actor gave a performance while drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plastered' is slang for drunk, but here it means coated with plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Rendered means performed a piece of music or drama, and also means a wall was coated with a first layer of plaster.

clue.text: Poles with an urge to inform

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
an itch is a restless urge

explanation.surface: Poles feel an urge to tell the authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' are not people from Poland: they are the North and South poles, N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: To snitch is slang for telling tales or informing on someone.

clue.text: Hit man at home following a couple of idiots

indicators.note: following means the piece for at home comes after the other pieces
a couple means two, so the word for idiot appears twice

parts.note: an ass is a fool or idiot
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: A contract killer waits at home after two fools have left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a couple of' doubles the fool, and 'following' puts the at-home word after the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a hired killer of a public figure.

clue.text: Second pick? That's a laugh

parts.note: the pick of something is its best part, its cream

explanation.surface: Someone choosing again laughs off the second pick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pick' is a noun meaning the best of the bunch, the cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hilarious is called a scream, a real source of amusement.

clue.text: Free gin being served up

parts.note: to rid is to free, as in rid of pests

indicators.note: gin being served is poured out and mixed, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Free gin is on offer at the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is the definition: in horse racing a jockey who is 'up' is mounted on the horse. 'being served' rearranges GIN as ING.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing language a jockey up is mounted, sitting astride the horse.

clue.text: Carry on with summary

explanation.surface: Someone continues with a brief summary.
explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to continue after a pause, and a resume is a short summing-up or CV.

clue.text: Decides to barter, as it is damaged

indicators.note: something damaged is broken up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone decides to swap goods since the item is damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges BARTER AS IT.
explanation.definitionFit: To arbitrate is to judge or settle a dispute.

clue.text: Job centre before people sign

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: men are people

explanation.surface: The Job Centre comes before the people sign on for benefits.
explanation.walkthrough: A Job Centre is a British state employment office; here 'centre' takes O from 'Job'.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent, a sign of what is to come.

clue.text: Complete, and almost open

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden

explanation.surface: Something is finished and almost open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter T from OVERT.
explanation.definitionFit: When something is over it is finished and done.

clue.text: Entrance to a university is a piece of cake

parts.note: a gate is a way in, an entrance

explanation.surface: Getting into university is easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece of cake' usually means something easy; here it is literal, a rich cream cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich layered cream sponge, served in slices.

clue.text: Obstructed by case of head adopting current measure

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the outside letters wrap round the next piece
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: the ampere is the unit measuring electric current

explanation.surface: Someone is held back by having to measure electric current with their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes H and D from 'head', and 'adopting' puts AMPERE inside them.
explanation.definitionFit: To be hampered is to be hindered or held back.
